newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ruling ANC rejects cabinet change talk.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ruling ANC rejects cabinet change talk.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress on Tuesday rejected speculation about a possible cabinet reshuffle as racist and uninformed.

President Nelson Mandela's ANC said in a statement the speculation was an attempt to undermine efforts to unite South Africans behind the government's post-apartheid reconstruction and development programme and its macroeconomic strategy.

"Those responsible hope to undermine the huge strides the government had undertaken in the implementation of the macroeconomic strategy, with a specific racist focus on (Finance) Minister Trevor Manuel," the statment said.

Government officials earlier scotched market rumours that Manuel, who is black, was about to be replaced by Alec Erwin, the white trade and industry minister, as part of cabinet changes early next month.
A spokesman for Mandela reiterated on Monday there were no imminent plans for replacing the finance minister.
The ANC, the majority party in the government of national unity, said it continued to believe in a collective approach to the tasks facing the country.
"The ANC remains convinced that the cabinet in its entirety is on track in achieving its goals," it said.

Rumours of the reshuffle began with newspaper reports last week about the possible retirement of several cabinet ministers. These suggested that Erwin was likely to replace Manuel, although some dealers said there were also rumours that Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus might be promoted.
Manuel was tipped to be moved to the Foreign Ministry.
The rand came under attack on Monday on jitters sparked by the rumours, but the currency strengthened sharply in early trade on Tuesday morning as foreign and local market players sold dollars.
A stronger bond market and easier money market conditions also helped it to gain nearly four cents, to trade around the 4.66 level against the dollar.
